nodes.description: A patent document titled "Real-time ad-hoc spam filtering of email" describing a multi-pass ad-hoc spam message filtering approach that dynamically generates a temporary classifier.

nodes.entity_id: Multi-Pass Ad-Hoc Spam Message Filtering Approach
nodes.description: A filtering approach that dynamically generates a temporary classifier during a first pass based on results of a previously applied message filter that sorts messages into folders, then uses the classifier in a second pass to retrospectively inspect messages and present potentially misclassified messages to the user.
nodes.id: Multi-Pass Ad-Hoc Spam Message Filtering Approach

nodes.description: A message filter used by a network device to assign messages to different message folders and configured to store first classification data in a persistent store; it is automatically executed independent of a user action.<SEP>A previously applied message filter that sorts messages into a plurality of different message folders and is configured to store first classification data in a persistent store.

A multi-pass message filter configured to generate a classification model based on a first pass analysis, perform a second pass to generate misclassification identification, and employ a Naive Bayes classifier.

A model generated by the multi-pass message filter during a first pass, configured to reside exclusively in a non-persistent memory location on a user's client device and not stored on disk or another persistent data store.
Classification data generated by the first message filter and stored in a persistent store.<SEP>Classification data stored in a persistent store by the first message filter.

Classification data generated by the first pass of the multi-pass message filter to train it, residing exclusively in a non-persistent memory store at the client device and deleted upon providing the display of information.<SEP>Classification data generated by the first pass of the multi-pass message filter, configured to reside exclusively in a non-persistent memory store and be deleted so it is no longer accessible.
A plurality of different folders into which messages are sorted by the first message filter, used to train the multi-pass message filter based on which folder each message resides.

An identification of sorted messages that might be misclassified, generated by the second pass of the multi-pass message filter and displayed so a user can move misclassified messages to different folders.

A device configured to receive messages, assign them to different message folders using the first message filter, and communicate the messages over the network to the message folders.<SEP>A device comprising a transceiver to send and receive data over a network and a processor operative to perform the multi-pass message filtering actions.

A device configured to execute the multi-pass message filter, generate second classification data in a non-persistent memory store, score messages, identify incorrectly sorted messages, and provide a display of information enabling a user to move messages.<SEP>A user's device on which the classification model is maintained in memory and on which the first and second passes of the multi-pass message filter may execute entirely.
A medium including data and instructions whose execution on a computing device provides for managing messages via the multi-pass message filtering actions.
A classifier employed by the multi-pass message filter.

A memory store at the client device where the second classification data resides exclusively.<SEP>A memory location in which the generated classification model resides exclusively, from which it is purged and not stored on disk or another persistent data store.
A storage location where the first message filter stores first classification data.<SEP>A persistent data store in which the first message filter stores first classification data.

A communication item received in plurality, assigned to message folders, scored by the multi-pass message filter, and potentially identified as sorted into an incorrect message folder.<SEP>An email message received over a network, sorted into folders, and analyzed for spam filtering, including sender information, headers, subject, originating network address, contents, and attachments.

A person enabled to move an identified message to another message folder, who may select the multi-pass message filter for execution through an interface on the client device.<SEP>A person whose mail folders are scanned and who is presented a list of potentially misclassified messages and enabled to move identified messages to another folder.

A message filter executed in multiple passes on sorted messages at a client device, trained by generating second classification data in a first pass and used in a second pass to score each message and identify messages sorted into incorrect message folders.
A folder to which messages are assigned and sorted; a message may be identified as stored in an incorrect message folder and moved to another message folder.
An address book associated with a recipient that is associated with the message folders, used in analysis for generating second classification data.
An interface on the client device through which a user can select the multi-pass message filter for execution.

edges.description: The first message filter sorts messages into a plurality of different message folders.
The first message filter is configured to store first classification data in a persistent store.
The network device assigns messages to message folders using the first message filter.<SEP>The first message filter is configured to execute on a network device distinct from a client device.
The second multi-pass message filter generates the classification model and uses it to perform a second pass.
The first pass of the multi-pass message filter trains it by generating second classification data.
The multi-pass message filter employs a Naive Bayes classifier.
The second pass of the multi-pass message filter generates a misclassification identification of sorted messages.
The first and second passes of the multi-pass message filter occur entirely on a client device.
Execution of instructions on the storage medium enables the multi-pass message filter actions for managing messages.
The network device's processor performs the first and second pass analysis using the second multi-pass message filter.
The generated classification model is configured to reside exclusively in a non-persistent memory location.
The classification model is maintained within memory on a user's client device.
The classification model is generated based on an analysis of at least which message folder a message currently resides.
The first classification data is stored in a persistent store.

The second classification data is configured to reside exclusively in a non-persistent memory store at the client device.<SEP>The second classification data is configured to reside exclusively in a non-persistent memory store.
The second classification data is deleted from the client device upon providing the display of information.
The first pass of the multi-pass message filter trains the filter by generating second classification data.
The second classification data is generated based on analysis of whether a message sender's address is in an address book associated with a recipient.
The second classification data is generated based on which folder each of the plurality of messages resides.
The message folders contain messages previously sorted by the first message filter.
The message folders are associated with a recipient user.
The misclassification identification is displayed to the user so misclassified messages can be moved to different folders.
The network device receives a plurality of messages and assigns them to different message folders.<SEP>The network device manages a delivery of a message over a network.
The network device communicates the messages over the network to the plurality of different message folders.
The client device executes a first pass and a second pass of the multi-pass message filter on the sorted messages.
The client device identifies any message whose score indicates it is sorted into an incorrect message folder.
The client device provides a display of information associated with incorrectly sorted messages such that a user is enabled to move the identified message.
Using the second classification data, the second pass of the multi-pass message filter scores each message.
The user is enabled to move the identified message to another message folder.
The multi-pass message filter is selectable for execution by a user through an interface on the client device.
